transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (HaloGrid Partnerships), Liam O'Neill (HaloGrid Channel), Priya Kapoor (HaloGrid Solutions), Derek Tan (HaloGrid CRO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
- Alignment on co-sell GTM, prioritization of two anchor pilots, definition of partner attachment rules, and an ask for a low-touch tech benchmark.
- Key risks flagged: data residency in EMEA, SOC2 attestation timeline, and potential displacement by DatumAI on price.

Topics: pipeline mapping, revenue split, technical gating, compliance checklist, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Sofia Alvarez: Hi, Sofia here. Head of Partnerships at HaloGrid.
[00:11] Liam O'Neill: Liam, channel sales.
[00:13] Priya Kapoor: Priya, solutions architect.
[00:15] Derek Tan: Derek, CRO.
[00:17] Omar Patel: Omar, SE from Redwood.
[00:19] Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda — we want to align on the co-sell wiring, ops for pipeline handoff and identify two pilot deals to run technical bench on. Roughly 45 minutes then wrap.

[02:05] Sofia Alvarez: Quick context — HaloGrid has a set of telco customers that are asking for low-latency embedding search and private inference. We think Redwood is a strong fit but we need clear rules for partner credits, joint account planning, and support SLA expectations.

[03:10] Maya Chen: Understood. From Redwood side, typical flow is AE introduces, we do a joint tech scoping with SE, and for pilots we can offer a discounted reserved capacity or burst credits depending on the use case. Omar — can you walk through the tech gating?

[04:02] Omar Patel: Sure. Two quick buckets — hosted API and private deployments. Hosted is fastest to launch, lower ops for HaloGrid and customer, but has multi-tenant constraints and may not meet strict data residency needs. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives isolation and KMS control but longer lead time — provisioning, network peering, and compliance checks. For telco, latency and data locality are common blockers.

[06:30] Liam O'Neill: Pricing question — how do we avoid getting eaten by DatumAI? They undercut list price but we need clear margins for HaloGrid to push the deal.

[07:05] Maya Chen: We do two things — partner referral credits and co-sell uplift. We can structure a 10–15% partner credit for first-year committed spend plus marketing development funds for enterprise pilots. We'll share a templated spreadsheet.

[08:20] Priya Kapoor: From a gating perspective we need SOC2 Level II evidence, SSO via SAML, audit logs export, and per-tenant encryption keys (KMS) for at-rest. Also data residency for EMEA tenants. Do you support HSM integration?

[09:03] Omar Patel: We integrate with major KMS providers; HSM support depends on private deployment packaging — yes for on-prem and certain VPC setups. Audit logs and token-level tracing exist via the Console. Note: our SOC2 report is in progress — attestation expected Q4 2026.

[11:40] Derek Tan: That's tight, we have one EMEA customer with procurement requiring SOC2 within 60 days. Is there a workaround?

[12:05] Maya Chen: Short term we can offer contractual commitments around data handling plus an exemption path where HaloGrid retains written attestation from customer legal. But long term, SOC2 is recommended. We'll flag this as a risk for that specific deal.

[14:00] Sofia Alvarez: On the pipeline — we have three likely opportunities:
- Deal A: telco analytics pilot (EMEA) — close intent Q4
- Deal B: vertical search for insurance broker — US, pricing-sensitive
- Deal C: retail personalization POC — APAC, later in Q1

[15:10] Maya Chen: Great. Which two should we prioritize for co-sell pilots? My read: Deal A (due to strategic footprint) and Deal B (revenue velocity).

[16:30] Liam O'Neill: Agreed. For Deal B the customer already uses NimbusCloud — they care a lot about cost per inference. Do you have suggestions around quantization/throughput that we can pitch?

[17:05] Omar Patel: Yes — Redwood Optimize recommendations: lower precision quantization, batching, and prefix KV caching for the search workflow. We can produce a cost estimate delta vs baseline Nimbus numbers if HaloGrid shares typical qps and latency SLOs.

[19:22] Priya Kapoor: We need that estimate to be conservative; procurement will use it against Nimbus. Also, how do you handle model version pinning and rollbacks during a pilot?

[20:05] Omar Patel: We support pin-by-version and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback. We log metrics and provide per-route dashboards so we can detect regressions and rollback quickly.

[22:00] Liam O'Neill: Any deep tech risk around KV cache and stateful serving if we do multi-tenant hosted?

[22:18] Omar Patel: There's a throughput vs isolation tradeoff — continuous batching is efficient but for strict isolation we recommend dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated) which we can provision for pilots on a short-term commit.

[24:40] Derek Tan: Commercial ask — what does a short-term dedicated pool look like? Minimum commit?

[25:05] Maya Chen: Typical short pilots can be done with a month commitment and a small reserved capacity; pricing varies by GPU class. We'll put non-binding numbers in the spreadsheet.

[27:10] Sofia Alvarez: Operationally, who will be the single-threaded owner on Redwood side for onboarding and runbook handover?

[27:28] Maya Chen: That will be Omar for tech, and I'll own commercial ops. We'll loop in Customer Success once pilot terms are signed.

[29:00] Priya Kapoor: On security checklist — can you provide log export format? We need to map to our SIEM. Also retention policy for logs.

[29:22] Omar Patel: Exports are JSON lines via S3 or webhook. Retention configurable; default is 90 days in Console but we can extend for enterprise plans.

[31:10] Liam O'Neill: Competitor angle — DatumAI doesn't offer a private deployment option in our region, Nimbus offers price leadership but limited model catalog. How do we position Redwood?

[31:40] Maya Chen: Position on predictable economics, private deployment, and observability — we emphasize unit-cost controls (batching, cache), plus a dev-friendly integration for quick POCs.

[33:50] Sofia Alvarez: On co-sell motions, HaloGrid needs a referral template and a joint marketing plan. We also want a shared lead routing process in CRM — who owns the initial contact?

[34:18] Maya Chen: Suggested routing: HaloGrid fills basic lead form + intro email, AE (Maya) owns qualification, then SE (Omar) does scoping. We'll circulate a one-pager of that flow.

[36:05] Priya Kapoor: For the technical benchmark, can Redwood run a sample eval on our anonymized logs? We can mask PII. Need latency and cost per 1k requests.

[36:40] Omar Patel: Yes — lightweight benchmark on hosted infra is fastest. If we need isolation, we can spin up a dedicated pool but that adds time. We'll ask for sample qps and request payloads.

[38:55] Derek Tan: Can we discuss success criteria — what counts as a win for HaloGrid and Redwood after pilot?

[39:20] Sofia Alvarez: HaloGrid win: 20% reduction in inference cost vs current vendor and a signed statement of technical fit for telco use-cases. Redwood win: a path to $X committed ARR and marketing case study.

[40:30] Maya Chen: Agreed. We'll document measurable KPIs: latency p95 < 200ms for search, cost per 1k tokens < $Y, and security gating satisfied.

[42:00] Liam O'Neill: Procurement and legal — will Redwood accept HaloGrid's partner addendum or you need your own? Also, SSO and SCIM support?

[42:33] Maya Chen: We have a partner addendum template; we can consume HaloGrid's changes if it's within standard risk parameters. SCIM and SAML are supported. For any bespoke contractual asks, we'll engage legal.

[44:10] Priya Kapoor: One more tech nit — do you support per-route cost attribution so we can invoice customers separate pieces?

[44:28] Omar Patel: Yes, Console has token-level cost and per-route breakdowns. We can also push usage reports to S3 for billing reconciliation.

[46:05] Sofia Alvarez: Risk register — I want to capture the EMEA SOC2 timing, potential price push by DatumAI, and Nimbus's incumbent relationship. Can Redwood provide an escalation path if a deal stalls?

[46:34] Maya Chen: We'll assign a stall-remediation owner (Maya) and a weekly sync cadence for stuck deals; escalation to Sales Leadership at 14 days no-progress.

[48:00] Omar Patel: Quick note on benchmarks — we'll produce a conservative cost/latency estimate and an optimistic one. Use conservative for procurement.

[49:12] Derek Tan: Sounds good. Anything else from HaloGrid?

[49:20] Sofia Alvarez: No, just want clear attachments — who signs pilots, and the revenue split. We'll review your template.

[50:01] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to share co-sell one-pager, pilot pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 timeline note, and tech benchmark template. HaloGrid to nominate two pilots and provide anonymized payloads. Action owners captured.

[51:10] Liam O'Neill: I'll send the intro emails for the pilot customers by Friday.
[51:25] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
